name: com.tetheredtrust/tethered-trust
title: Tethered Trust
description: Fit, compatibility and recall checks for AI agents before they buy: verdicts, evidence, receipts.

tools.name: how_it_works
tools.description: What Tethered Trust is, what it covers, where its data comes from, pricing and terms.

tools.name: list_coverage
tools.description: Which product categories and models are in the compatibility graph, with counts. Pass a category to list its models. Covers anything that has to fit, plug in, mount, run on or charge with something someone owns. Verified catalog (specs checked against cited manufacturer sources): computers & consoles (RAM, M.2 SSDs, USB-C chargers), phones/tablets/watches (USB-C PD, MagSafe, Qi2, watch bands), cameras (lens mounts, adapters, batteries, memory cards), cordless power tools (battery platforms), printers (ink, toner, drums), appliances (refrigerator water and air filters, dryer vents and power cords, installation fit), vacuums (bags, filters, batteries, robot-vacuum parts), air quality (purifier filters, HVAC media, humidifier pads), e-bikes (batteries and chargers by drive system), smart home (Matter, Thread, Zigbee, hubs, bulb bases), PC building (CPU sockets, cooler mounts, memory, clearances, power), cars & EV charging (tire sizes by trim, NACS/J1772/CCS1 and approved adapters, home chargers; a starter set of models) and TVs, consoles & streaming (VESA mounts, weight and screen size, console generations, app platforms). Products outside the catalog in any category are read by AI in terms of the same standards and returned as unverified.

category.description: Optional: one category id from a previous list_coverage call (e.g. 'cameras') to list every model in it.

tools.name: check_cart_before_checkout
tools.description: Checks a cart at checkout. Takes the checkout session exactly as a commerce protocol returns it (a UCP checkout or an ACP CheckoutSession) or plain line items, plus what the customer already owns. Returns a decision per line item, safe_to_checkout, an action (proceed, resolve_conditions, do_not_checkout, ask_customer), questions, substitutions, a signed receipt, and a com.tetheredtrust.shopping.compatibility extension object to attach to the checkout.

checkout.description: The checkout session as your commerce protocol returns it: a UCP checkout (line_items[].item.title) or an ACP CheckoutSession (line_items[].item.id). Or send line_items directly.

line_items.description: Generic cart: [{id, title | url | gtin | sku | text, quantity, price_usd}]. Used when checkout isn't sent.

cart_total_usd.description: Optional cart total in US dollars. Carts of $500 or more get a high_value notice to confirm with the manufacturer first.

products.description: ACP only: map of item id → {title | url | gtin} from your product feed, because ACP line items carry only ids.

owned.description: What the customer already owns that these items must work with (model numbers, URLs or descriptions; objects may carry config like memory_modules).

tools.name: identify_product
tools.description: Call this when the person gives a shop link, ASIN, barcode or vague product name and you need the exact model and what it's compatible with. Identify a product from a URL, model number, SKU, ASIN, UPC/EAN or description, and get its compatibility profile: the standards it takes and provides (mounts, sockets, connectors, platforms, part numbers, sizes), numeric limits (OS version, watts, weight, screen size), evidence and freshness. Products not in our reviewed catalog are researched on demand from the manufacturer's page and returned with status read_from_manufacturer_page (unreviewed) or unconfirmed (not enough to decide on). Use first when the product could be anything.

product.description: Anything that identifies the product: a manufacturer or retailer URL, a model number, SKU, ASIN, UPC/EAN, a vehicle VIN, or a listing title / description.

role.description: Optional: is this something the person already owns, or something being considered? Helps when a product is both (a phone owns cases; a car mount holds phones).

research.description: Default true. Set false to look only in the reviewed catalog (no on-demand research).

tools.name: list_standards
tools.description: Call this before sending products described by their specs instead of model numbers (e.g. specs_from or a custom product), or to map your own catalog fields onto ours: returns every standard family with its reviewed values (lens mounts, battery platforms, memory types, connectors, filters), the formats for new values and the numeric limit keys. Not needed for normal checks with model numbers. Free, read-only.

tools.name: resolve_product
tools.description: Call this to confirm exactly which model the person means before checking or buying ("which Galaxy S25 is this?") or to read a product's structured specs: looks it up by name or model number and returns its specs, what it accepts (mounts, battery platforms, cartridges, protocols) and what it fits. When the text matches several models it returns them all as candidates (ambiguous: true) so you can ask the person which one. For a yes/no fit answer use check_compatibility instead.

tools.name: validate_purchase_plan
tools.description: Call this before you recommend or order two or more items that have to work together or with what the person owns (a PC build or upgrade, a camera kit, a smart-home setup, a charger plus cable). Check a whole purchase before recommending or ordering it: the setup the person owns (with current configuration) plus everything in the cart. Returns one decision (supported / conditional / incompatible / insufficient_evidence), a result per part, configuration limits across the plan (memory slots and capacity, M.2 slots), adapters or hubs still needed, substitutions for parts that won't work, the exact questions blocking a decision, evidence, and a signed receipt. Covers anything that has to fit, plug in, mount, run on or charge with something someone owns. Verified catalog (specs checked against cited manufacturer sources): computers & consoles (RAM, M.2 SSDs, USB-C chargers), phones/tablets/watches (USB-C PD, MagSafe, Qi2, watch bands), cameras (lens mounts, adapters, batteries, memory cards), cordless power tools (battery platforms), printers (ink, toner, drums), appliances (refrigerator water and air filters, dryer vents and power cords, installation fit), vacuums (bags, filters, batteries, robot-vacuum parts), air quality (purifier filters, HVAC media, humidifier pads), e-bikes (batteries and chargers by drive system), smart home (Matter, Thread, Zigbee, hubs, bulb bases), PC building (CPU sockets, cooler mounts, memory, clearances, power), cars & EV charging (tire sizes by trim, NACS/J1772/CCS1 and approved adapters, home chargers; a starter set of models) and TVs, consoles & streaming (VESA mounts, weight and screen size, console generations, app platforms). Products outside the catalog in any category are read by AI in terms of the same standards and returned as unverified.

goal.description: Optional: what the person is trying to do, e.g. 'upgrade this laptop to 32 GB'. Echoed back; requirements are derived from the devices.

text.description: Exact model number or name, or key specs.

id.description: Exact product id (from resolve_product or a question's options).

for.description: Purchases only: which item this part is for (index or name), when the plan has several devices.

config.description: Setup items only: current configuration, e.g. {"memory_modules": [{"capacity_gb": 8}], "installed_drives": 1, "replace_memory": true}.

setup.description: What the person already owns (devices, appliances, tools, hubs) with exact model numbers, plus current configuration.

tools.name: fix_purchase_plan
tools.description: When a plan comes back incompatible or conditional: the smallest set of changes that makes it work (swap a part for a verified one that fits everything else, add a missing cooler, hub or adapter, trim quantities that exceed slots), re-validated, with the reason for each change. Fewest changes and verified products first; no prices.

tools.name: plan_upgrade
tools.description: Call this when the person asks what they can upgrade or add to a device they own ("can I add more RAM to my laptop", "what SSD does my PC take", "what GPU fits my case") before suggesting parts: returns memory type, slots and maximum, M.2 slots, lengths and PCIe generation, power, CPU and cooler support for motherboards, GPU and cooler clearance for cases, the parts in our graph that fit (verified first) and the manufacturer's notes. Pass the exact model.

model.description: The device's exact model number or name (laptop, motherboard, case, camera, tool...).

goal.description: Optional: what the person wants, e.g. 'more memory for video editing'.

tools.name: identify_from_photo
tools.description: Read the brand, model and part numbers from a photo of a label or nameplate and match them to products. Matches are returned as candidates, with what was read. The photo isn't stored.

image.description: A photo of the label or nameplate as a data URL (data:image/jpeg;base64,...), under 4 MB.

hint.description: Optional context, e.g. 'refrigerator label inside the door'.

tools.name: recheck_plan
tools.description: Re-run a saved purchase plan against today's data before ordering, and see what changed since it was issued: decisions, product records, or receipt status.

tools.name: check_batch
tools.description: Up to 25 independent compatibility checks in one call (e.g. ranking candidate products for one device). Each result has its own decision, evidence and receipt.

existing.description: What the person already has, ideally with the exact model number, e.g. 'Lenovo ThinkPad T480', 'Sony A7 IV', 'DeWalt DCD800', 'HP OfficeJet Pro 9015e', 'iPhone 16 Pro', 'HomePod mini'.

candidate.description: What they want to buy: a model/part number or key specs, e.g. 'Crucial CT16G4SFRA32A', '1TB M.2 2230 NVMe', 'DCB205', 'HP 962XL', 'Canon RF 24-105mm f/4L', 'Eve Energy'.

detail.description: Optional extra identifiers: machine type, revision, year, region, serial range.

existing_id.description: Optional: an exact product id (from resolve_product, suggestions or a candidates list) instead of existing text.

candidate_id.description: Optional: an exact product id instead of candidate text.

tools.name: check_compatibility
tools.description: Call this whenever you're about to recommend, link to or buy a part, accessory, charger, filter, cartridge, lens, battery, memory, mount or adapter for something the person already owns, or they ask "will X work with Y" / "is this compatible". Pass both exact models. Covers anything that has to fit, plug in, mount, run on or charge with something someone owns (list_coverage shows the verified catalog). Returns a decision (supported / conditional / incompatible / insufficient_evidence), the rules checked, caveats, required accessories, the questions to ask when it can't decide, evidence links and a signed receipt. When the text matches several models it returns each candidate's answer.

existing.description: What the person already has, ideally with the exact model number, e.g. 'Lenovo ThinkPad T480', 'Sony A7 IV', 'DeWalt DCD800', 'HP OfficeJet Pro 9015e', 'iPhone 16 Pro', 'HomePod mini'.

candidate.description: What they want to buy: a model/part number or key specs, e.g. 'Crucial CT16G4SFRA32A', '1TB M.2 2230 NVMe', 'DCB205', 'HP 962XL', 'Canon RF 24-105mm f/4L', 'Eve Energy'.

detail.description: Optional extra identifiers: machine type, revision, year, region, serial range.

existing_id.description: Optional: an exact product id (from resolve_product, suggestions or a candidates list) instead of existing text.

candidate_id.description: Optional: an exact product id instead of candidate text.

tools.name: find_parts
tools.description: Call this when the person names a device or appliance they own and needs a replacement or add-on ("what filter does my fridge take", "which RAM can I add", "what battery fits my drill") before you search shops or guess. Which parts and accessories fit this model? OEM parts first, then verified alternatives: e.g. a refrigerator's water filter, a printer's cartridges, a camera's lenses and batteries, a tool's batteries, or the RAM, SSDs and chargers that fit a computer.

model.description: Model number of the device, tool, camera, printer or appliance, e.g. 'GFE28GYNFS', 'ThinkPad T480', 'Canon EOS R6 Mark II', 'Milwaukee 2904-20', 'Brother HL-L2350DW'.

tools.name: check_recalls
tools.description: Call this before recommending, buying or selling anything used or secondhand, any baby or kids' product, appliance, heater, battery-powered device or vehicle, or when the person asks if something is safe or recalled. Searches US government recall notices: CPSC for consumer products (appliances, furniture, kids' products, electronics, tools; by brand and model or UPC) and NHTSA for vehicles (by year, make and model). Use before buying, selling or recommending something, especially used or secondhand. Returns decision (recalled / possible_recall / no_recall_found / insufficient_evidence) with each notice's hazard, remedy, which units it applies to and the official link. 'no_recall_found' is not a safety guarantee.

product.description: Brand and model as on the label or listing, e.g. 'Graco SnugRide 35', 'Ninja AF101', 'Arlopu KT-CS17 slide playset'. Model numbers matter: send them when you have them.

brand.description: Optional: the brand, if not in product.

model.description: Optional: the exact model number, if not in product.

vehicle.description: For cars and motorcycles: year, make and model, e.g. '2023 Tesla Model Y'. Or send make, model and year separately.

tools.name: watch_decision
tools.description: Call this after a compatibility check, purchase plan, verify_page or verify_mcp result that someone will rely on later (an order next week, an install, a resale, the next agent in a handoff). For product decisions we watch the records, manufacturer sources and US recall notices behind it; for page and MCP checks we re-run the same checks daily. Watches last 30 days and need only the receipt_id. Free during early access.

receipt_id.description: The receipt id (rcpt_...) that came with a check_compatibility or validate_purchase_plan answer.

tools.name: attach_order
tools.description: Call this right after placing an order you checked with check_cart_before_checkout, validate_purchase_plan or check_compatibility: link the receipt_id to the order number, AP2 cart or intent mandate, ACP checkout session, UCP checkout or payment reference. This makes a Decision Record: if the purchase is ever disputed ("the agent bought the wrong thing"), anyone can show what was checked, from which sources, and what changed since. Free.

receipt_id.description: The receipt id (rcpt_...) from the check, plan or checkout check made before buying.

ap2_cart_mandate.description: AP2 cart mandate hash or id, if the purchase used AP2.

ap2_intent_mandate.description: AP2 intent mandate hash or id.

tools.name: dispute_packet
tools.description: Call this when an agent purchase is disputed, returned as wrong, or charged back and a Tethered Trust receipt exists for it: we assemble the evidence (the decision, products checked, sources with dates, the linked order or mandate, records and recall notices that changed since, reported outcomes, and signature verification) into one printable page and JSON anyone can verify. For merchants, platforms and buyers. $1.50 per packet.

receipt_id.description: The receipt id (rcpt_...) of the decision made before the purchase.

tools.name: file_claim
tools.description: Call this when a product we said would work didn't (within 60 days of the check): send the receipt_id and what happened. Decided within 10 business days; if our answer or data was wrong, the fee paid for that check is refunded and the data corrected. Free. For a plain fit/no-fit report without a claim, use report_outcome.

receipt_id.description: The receipt id (rcpt_...) of the check that was wrong.

what_happened.description: What was bought, what it was used with, and what didn't work.

evidence_url.description: Optional link to a photo, the order or a manufacturer page showing the problem.

tools.name: decision_status
tools.description: Call this right before acting on a watched decision: still_holds, changed (a record it rested on was updated), recall_on_record (a recall notice names one of the products), or expired, with what changed and what isn't monitored.

receipt_id.description: Or the receipt id that was watched.

tools.name: check_fit
tools.description: Will this appliance physically fit this space? Compares dimensions plus typical installation clearances and required connections (power, water, gas).

product.description: What's being installed, e.g. '36-inch French-door refrigerator'. Used to pick typical clearances.

product_dimensions.description: Width, height and depth of the product (from its spec sheet). Any subset is accepted; missing axes come back as 'missing'.

width.description: A number in inches (e.g. "35.75") or text with units ("35 3/4 in", "90.8 cm", "908 mm").

height.description: A number in inches (e.g. "35.75") or text with units ("35 3/4 in", "90.8 cm", "908 mm").

depth.description: A number in inches (e.g. "35.75") or text with units ("35 3/4 in", "90.8 cm", "908 mm").

opening.description: Width, height and depth of the space it goes into. Any subset is accepted; missing axes come back as 'missing'.

width.description: A number in inches (e.g. "35.75") or text with units ("35 3/4 in", "90.8 cm", "908 mm").

height.description: A number in inches (e.g. "35.75") or text with units ("35 3/4 in", "90.8 cm", "908 mm").

depth.description: A number in inches (e.g. "35.75") or text with units ("35 3/4 in", "90.8 cm", "908 mm").

needs.description: Connections the product needs, e.g. '120V, water line' or '240V'.

tools.name: verify_receipt
tools.description: Check a Tethered Trust receipt: is the signature ours, is it still within valid_until, and have the records behind it changed since? A valid receipt proves what we said and when; it doesn't guarantee the verdict was right.

receipt_id.description: The receipt id (rcpt_...) from a check.

jws.description: Or the full signed receipt string, if someone handed it to you.

tools.name: report_outcome
tools.description: After a purchase, report whether it actually fit. Free, safe to call, and only the first report per check counts. Reports are weighted by level: self_reported (website), agent_reported (anonymous API/MCP), partner_reported (API key holders) and order_confirmed (order evidence we've confirmed). Only the last two can raise future confidence.

check_id.description: The check_id returned by check_compatibility, find_parts or check_fit, or the check_id on an item or result of validate_purchase_plan.

evidence.description: Optional order details we can confirm later (raises the report to 'order_confirmed' once reviewed). Order references only; payment and personal details aren't accepted.
